R. Q. 1 يَأْيَأَهُ , inf. n. يَأْيَأَهٌ and يَأْيَآءٌ, [respecting the form of which latter see ظَأْظَأَ,] He made a show of kindness, benignity, or favour to him. (K.) ―
-b2- إِنَّمَا هُوَ يَأْيَآءٌ [It is only making a show of kindness, &c.: or, perhaps, He is only one who makes a show of kindness, &c,]. (L.) ＝
-A2- يَأْيَأَ بِالقَوْمِ He called the people: (K: so too in the L, and this is the correct meaning: TA:) or he said to the people يَأَّيَأَّ, in order that they should assemble, or collect together. (K) ―
-b2- يَأْيَأَ بِالإِبِلِ He called to the camels by the cry أَىْ, (whence the verb is formed by transposition, TA,) to quiet them. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
